title: One-component Ext degree characterization
statement: A bounded projective resolution of a module is equivalent to vanishing of Ext in degree n + 1 against every module: for every commutative ring R, module X, and natural n, HasProjectiveResolutionLE X n ↔ ∀ Y : ModuleCat (max u v) R, Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext X Y (n + 1)) using HasExt.standard.

proof.text: Forward implication: unpack a projective resolution P supported in degrees at most n. Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.extMk_surjective represents every class in Ext^(n+1)(X,Y) by a cocycle from P_(n+1). That term is zero, so the cocycle is zero and extMk_zero makes the class zero. Any two classes therefore agree.

Reverse implication: induct on n, generalizing X. For n=0 the projective Ext-one criterion makes X projective. ProjectiveResolution.self X is a resolution concentrated in degree zero, hence has the required bound.

For the successor case use the standard projective epimorphism Projective.π X and its kernel short exact sequence S. For a class a in Ext^(n+1)(S.X₁,Y), the connecting class in Ext^(n+2)(X,Y) is zero by the hypothesis. The contravariant long exact sequence writes a as the precomposition of a class from the projective S.X₂. That class is zero by positive-degree projective Ext vanishing. Thus the induction hypothesis supplies an actual bounded projective resolution Q of S.X₁.

Splice explicitly using ChainComplex.augment: put S.X₂ in degree zero and Q_i in degree i+1, with first differential Q.π.f 0 followed by S.f and augmentation S.g. ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono transports exactness from S to degree zero (Q.π.f 0 is epic), and from the cokernel presentation of Q to degree one (S.f is monic). Higher exactness is inherited from Q.

Build the projective resolution structure. In degree zero ChainComplex.quasiIsoAt₀_iff and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_zeros' identify the augmentation quasi-isomorphism condition with exactness and epimorphy. In every positive degree quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt' reduces it to the exactness just established. Projectivity follows term by term from S.X₂ and Q; the bound above n+1 follows by shifting the bound on Q. This completes the induction without postponed construction data.

proof_origin.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065R; direct cocycle proof of the forward direction and the explicit kernel-induction and splicing proof of the reverse direction (J4).

lean.statement: theorem projective_resolution_ext_degree {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (X : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (n : ℕ) : (HasProjectiveResolutionLE X n ↔ ∀ Y : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, Subsingleton (@Abelian.Ext _ _ _ (HasExt.standard (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) X Y (n + 1)))
